title: Backdoor Trigger Generalization Testing Using Semantic Variants

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct chain: mapping trigger generalization boundaries informs whether trigger-filtering defenses are sufficient. If safety-relevant backdoors generalize more broadly, this raises the threat level for covert malicious fine-tuning and motivates different defense strategies.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model with a planted backdoor, then systematically testing semantic variants. Fine-tuning requires GPU resources (medium compute helps) and ML pipeline expertise. Generating semantic variants (synonyms, paraphrases, translations, partial matches) and measuring generalization boundaries requires careful experimental design. Significant ML skills needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one backdoor technique and its generalization, which is reasonably narrow. However, the fine-tuning step + systematic variant testing + comparison between safety-relevant and task-performance backdoors adds up. Tight for 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
